original_names: Médaille commémorative de Madagascar — première expédition
period_scope: French Third Republic; first expedition 1883–1886; creating law 31 July 1886; the explicit diploma page labels the shown diploma as remis en 1886
granting_body: French Republic; law of 31 July 1886 created the commemorative medal for officers, soldiers, sailors and volunteers who took part in the Madagascar expedition

legal_records.official_reference: J.O. 5 August 1886, p. 3625 (as transcribed on the SAMLHOC page)
legal_records.effect: Instituted the Madagascar commemorative medal for the 1883–1886 expedition; SAMLHOC states that it used the same module and face as the Tonkin medal, with a Madagascar reverse and a ribbon of small horizontal green/blue stripes.
SAMLHOC records disciplinary rules applying to holders of the Madagascar commemorative medal.
SAMLHOC records the notice in its family-delivery sequence; no separate issue date is inferred.
SAMLHOC records the notice completing family-delivery arrangements under the 26 July 1887 law.

eligibility_summary: Participants in the first Madagascar expedition of 1883–1886; the page describes the corps operating at Majunga and Tamatave and states that attribution was accompanied by a diploma. The exact issue date of an individual medal is not inferred.
physical_description: Round silver medal, 30 mm, engraved by Jean-Baptiste Daniel Dupuis. Obverse: REPUBLIQUE FRANÇAISE around the helmeted Republic, PATRIE on the visor, surrounded by laurel. Reverse: a small star on rays framed by 1883 and 1886 above MADAGASCAR, over a trophy of four flags and a naval anchor, with laurel surround. SAMLHOC says the first medals used an oval suspension. Common ribbon: 36 mm, alternating horizontal blue and green stripes of 4 mm.

variants.label: Premières fabrications / attache de bélière ovoïde
variants.details: SAMLHOC explicitly states that the first medals were made with an oval suspension; this is a version of the same 1886 commemorative medal, not a new family.

variants.label: Ruban réglementaire bleu/vert
variants.details: SAMLHOC describes a 36 mm ribbon with alternating horizontal blue and green stripes, each 4 mm; the same ribbon description is given for both Madagascar medals.

original_names: Médaille commémorative de Madagascar — seconde expédition
period_scope: French Third Republic; second expedition 8 December 1894–31 December 1895, with occupation-corps extension 1 January–31 October 1896 under the law of 21 July 1897; the explicit diploma page labels the shown diploma as remis en 1898
granting_body: French Republic; law of 15 January 1896 created the medal for the second expedition and law of 21 July 1897 extended eligibility to the occupation corps through 31 October 1896

legal_records.official_reference: J.O. 17 January 1896, p. 273 (as transcribed on the SAMLHOC page)
legal_records.effect: Instituted the commemorative medal for service from 8 December 1894 through 31 December 1895; SAMLHOC includes military, naval, Senegalese auxiliary and Kabyle auxiliary eligibility and states that the medal retained the same metal/module while its reverse records army/navy collaboration.
Applied disciplinary rules to holders of the second-expedition Madagascar medal.

SAMLHOC records detailed delivery/administrative rules for Navy troops, including brevet, medal, ribbon and 1895 clasp; the page also notes an escort eligibility period of 26 October–21 November 1894.
Preparatory debate for extending the 1896 medal to the occupation corps.
Senate discussion of the bill extending the 1896 medal coverage.
Extended the same medal to military and naval personnel of the Madagascar occupation corps serving from 1 January through 31 October 1896.

eligibility_summary: The law of 15 January 1896 covered the second expedition from 8 December 1894 to 31 December 1895, including the named Senegalese and Kabyle auxiliaries recorded by SAMLHOC. The law of 21 July 1897 extended the same medal to the occupation corps through 31 October 1896. The exact issue date of an individual medal is not inferred; the diploma subpage separately labels the shown diploma as remis en 1898.
physical_description: Round silver medal, 30 mm, engraved by Louis Oscar Roty. Obverse: REPVBLIQVE FRANÇAISE around the helmeted Republic. Reverse: MADAGASCAR above a trophy of arms and the millesime 1895. The common ribbon is 36 mm with alternating horizontal blue and green stripes of 4 mm; SAMLHOC states that the ribbon for the 1895 medal carries a stylized silver laurel-leaf clasp with a 1895 scroll/date. The cached source image shows a complete obverse/reverse pair with that clasp.

variants.details: SAMLHOC explicitly describes the silver stylized laurel clasp bearing 1895; the object page labels the shown complete pair SECONDE EXPÉDITION.
